title: NEBExpress Ni Resin Batch Binding Protocol
author: New England Biolabs
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfd5ji86

steps.title: Prepare Buffers for Denaturing Conditions
steps.instruction: If using denaturing conditions, adjust Lysis/Binding, Wash, and Elution Buffers to a final concentration of 8 M Urea or 6 M Guanidine.

steps.title: Harvest Cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4000 x g for 15 minutes. Store the pellet at -20 °C or process immediately.

substeps.instruction: Pre-weigh the vessel prior to adding cell suspension to determine the mass of the cell pellet used.

steps.title: Lyse Cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in Lysis buffer (approximately 5 mL buffer per 1 g cell paste) and lyse using a chosen method (e.g., sonication, freeze-thaw cycles, French press, or commercial reagents).

substeps.instruction: Ensure imidazole is omitted from the lysis buffer.

steps.title: Clarify Lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 12000 x g for 15 minutes to pellet cellular debris.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the clarified protein lysate supernatant to a new microcentrifuge tube on ice.
Retain an aliquot of the clarified lysate for SDS-PAGE analysis.

steps.title: Prepare and Equilibrate Ni Resin
steps.instruction: Prepare the Ni Resin slurry and equilibrate it with Lysis/Binding buffer.

substeps.instruction: Gently shake the Ni Resin bottle to resuspend the slurry and transfer the desired amount to a tube.
Settle the resin by centrifugation at 500 x g for 5 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Equilibrate the resin by adding 5 column volumes (CV) of Lysis/Binding buffer and shake gently to mix.
Settle the resin again by centrifugation at 500 x g for 5 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Repeat the equilibration steps (adding 5 CV buffer and centrifuging) once more.

steps.title: Bind Protein to Resin
steps.instruction: Add the protein sample lysate to the equilibrated resin and mix by shaking at 200 rpm on a rotary shaker for ≥ 15 minutes.

substeps.instruction: If extending binding time, place resin at 4 °C to maintain target protein activity.

steps.title: Load Resin into Column
steps.instruction: Pour the lysate/resin mixture into an empty, closed gravity column.

substeps.instruction: Open the column and collect the flow-through in a clean tube for SDS-PAGE analysis.

steps.title: Wash Resin
steps.instruction: Add ≥ 10 CV of Wash buffer to the column and allow it to flow through.

substeps.instruction: Monitor flow-through with absorbance at 280 nm to ensure complete removal of unbound lysate.
Collect flow-through in fractions and reserve for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Note: Imidazole in wash buffer can be increased to 15 mM to reduce contaminants, though this may reduce yield.

steps.title: Elute Fusion Protein
steps.instruction: Elute the target protein using Elution buffer (minimum of 3 CV recommended).

substeps.instruction: Monitor protein elution by measuring absorbance at 280 nm or by SDS-PAGE.

steps.title: Analyze Samples
steps.instruction: Analyze the protein sample lysate (load), flow-through, washes, and eluates by SDS-PAGE.

substeps.instruction: To remove imidazole for downstream applications, use gel filtration (e.g., Zeba Spin Desalting Columns) or dialysis (e.g., slide-A-Lyzer Dialysis Cassettes).

steps.title: Clean Gravity Column
steps.instruction: Determine the flow rate prior to cleaning. Choose one of the following methods to remove contaminants:

substeps.instruction: To remove lipoproteins, lipids, and hydrophobic proteins: Add 1 M NaOH (contact time 1-2 hours), followed by 10 CV Lysis/Binding Buffer; OR add 30% isopropanol (contact time 15-20 minutes), followed by 10 CV water; OR add 0.1–0.5% non-ionic detergent in 0.1 M acetic acid (contact time 1-2 hours), followed by 10 CV water.
To remove proteins bound by ionic interactions: Add 1.5 M NaCl (contact time 10-15 minutes), followed by 10 CV water.

steps.title: Store Resin
steps.instruction: For long-term storage, store NEBExpress Ni Resin in 20% ethanol at 2 °C to 8 °C.
